blocks.text: Twenty focus areas become eighteen initiatives, one per focus area except where one owner delivers two.

The plan follows one chain from vision to measure. Each level answers a different question. The pillar says what must change and the focus area says where; the initiative says what Wesgro and its partners do, and the indicator says how Steerco will know it has happened (section 5.1).

blocks.caption: Seven levels run from the vision to the measures, and each level has a fixed count in this plan.

blocks.text: Two merges take twenty focus areas to eighteen initiatives. Segment-led marketing and mature-market yield share one owner and one set of channels, so focus areas 1 and 5 form initiative I1. Institutional alignment and industry collaboration share one forum, so focus areas 16 and 17 form I15. Every other focus area has its own initiative, numbered I1 to I18 in one sequence so that the M&E toolkit can track them on one list.

Leads are proposed, not agreed. They follow the Wesgro units named in the Inception Report's stakeholder map and the actions in Chapter 3, and Steerco confirms them at its first meeting [Steerco to confirm initiative leads and partners]. Six initiatives have a partner as the accountable lead, because the main lever sits outside Wesgro's mandate: corridor mobility, quality standards, flagship sites, community pilots, LTO funding and skills.
